newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Insurance holds firm in volatile 1996 market.
newsitem.headline: NZ Insurance holds firm in volatile 1996 market.

text.p: New Zealand Insurance -- the country's leading commercial and second largest consumer insurer -- recorded a 3.5 percent increase in gross written premiums to a record NZ$357.5 million for the 1996 year.
In its annual review released on Thursday the insurer recorded an increase of 66 percent in net underwriting profit, to NZ$15.6 million from $9.4 million.
Its combined underwriting and investment surplus before tax of $49 million was virtually steady versus 1995's NZ$49.1 million.

General manager Trevor Smith said in the review, "The insurance industry in New Zealand is highly competitive. New entrants have created an over-heated market which has led to unrealistic and unsustainable pricing.
"This is now resulting in unprofitability and market rationalisation which will create new opportunities that New Zealand Insurance is well placed to take advantage of."
The company believes that its strength in both commercial and consumer markets makes it less vulnerable to cyclical fluctuations in each one.
New Zealand Insurance's financial position means it is the only insurer to have built up a sizeable catastrophe provision, currently standing at NZ$15 million.

"This creates a cushioning against the impact on earnings of a severe earthquake or other disaster. Insurers who have not made appropriate provision are not serving the long-term interests of the customer or other stakeholders who are entitled to continuity of cover on reasonable terms," Smith said.
